gen-nixie-one-gf-albert-sans: Nostalgic and a bit retro-tech, Nixie One draws hairline curves with gaps left open, while Albert Sans holds its apertures clear down to tiny sizes. They feel like an old instrument panel next to a modern notebook.
gen-nixie-one-gf-alef: Alef reads as a modern, clean plain sans, its curves ending open all the way through. Nixie One does the showy part, with arches as thick as its stems, but Alef is the one you would actually settle into.
gen-nixie-one-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Contemporary and modern, Alegreya Sans SC opens its c wide. Nixie One has round letters with walls as heavy as the straight ones, so shrinking it much would start to feel cramped beside the body.
gen-nixie-one-gf-almarai: Nixie One brings a nostalgic, retro-tech look, with open curves and one constant stroke from top to baseline. Almarai follows with a line width that never swells or tapers, and letters that never seem to pinch shut.
gen-nixie-one-gf-amarna: Round, open curves and a constant stroke from top to baseline give Nixie One its retro-tech hum, a look that leans nostalgic. Amarna brings contrast-free strokes and unclogged small counters, which is the pair's strongest card.
gen-nixie-one-gf-andika: Professional and modern, Andika gives its tails and terminals the same heft as the main stems, with easy turns in the s. Nixie One's nostalgic, retro-tech hairlines sit above it, and a longer passage in Andika would read smoothly.
gen-nixie-one-gf-anta: That constant stroke from top to baseline, with open curves, gives Nixie One a nostalgic, retro-tech feel. Anta follows with gaping mouths on the e and a wire-bent sign look, so the heading deserves generous size.
gen-nixie-one-gf-antic: Nixie One looks nostalgic and retro-tech, its open curves held to a constant stroke from top to baseline. And Antic, drawn as if with a single nib, leaves its letter mouths open like unjoined chalk arcs, so a long passage would move along easily.
gen-nixie-one-gf-ar-one-sans: Thin rings and soft edges. Nixie One makes an o with a constant wall, while AR One Sans lifts its brush ends away before the curve closes, and that gentle, open quality is what this pairing does best.
gen-nixie-one-gf-assistant: Nixie One keeps its bold-looking and light-looking strokes from ever mixing inside a word, a nostalgic, retro-tech trait. And Assistant, a plain sans, holds its mouths open on c, e and a, so the heading earns its keep big and short.
